messages:
Maria Gomez: Hey team — customer (AcmeRetail) reporting intermittent failures when calling our private VPC endpoint through their enterprise proxy. They see successful CONNECT then the stream dies ~60s into the response and client gets "connection reset by peer". Logs attached show `RST_STREAM` from proxy and our side sees a short TLS write error. Repro steps they gave: 1) curl through corp proxy, 2) request a long streaming /chat completion that emits >2000 tokens. They say it only happens when proxy ALPN/HTTP2 interception is enabled. Any ideas?

Samir Patel: @Maria thanks — can you paste the customer curl and the minimal response logs? Also which proxy vendor/version?

Maria Gomez: curl they used: ```bash
curl -v --http2 --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/stream-chat
```
Proxy is BlueGate v6.2 (company says managed appliance). They captured tcpdump: shows successful CONNECT then a TLS ClientHello, our server responds, stream proceeds then after ~60s proxy sends TCP FIN, their client sees `recv: Connection reset by peer`. We also saw these in our access logs: `upstream prematurely closed connection` in proxy layer.

Alex Chen: Two quick hypotheses: (1) the proxy is doing HTTP/2 multiplexing/translation and is inserting an idle timeout on multiplexed streams; it might treat long lived streaming as idle if it rewrites ALPN. (2) the proxy may be terminating TLS for inspection and re-initiating upstream TLS with h2-to-h1 fallback or with altered keepalive semantics. Both can trigger premature close if keepalive/flow-control differs.

Samir Patel: Can the customer test forcing HTTP/1.1 for the CONNECT tunnel so we can see whether h2 proxying is the trigger? e.g. `curl --http1.1 --proxy ...` Also ask them to try adding a `Connection: keep-alive` header and/or disable proxy-level response buffering.

Maria Gomez: They tried `--http1.1` and said the stream stays open much longer, no reset after 5 minutes. So looks like h2 path is the issue. They also found a BlueGate setting `h2-connection-idle-timeout` set to 60s for multiplexed persistent connections.

Samir Patel: That explains it. For long-lived streaming we need the proxy to either increase the idle timeout or preserve the raw CONNECT stream (no h2 translation). Can we validate whether our client-side keepalive packets are visible to the proxy (i.e., is our NAT keepalive suppressed)? Also check if BlueGate rewrites ALPN from `h2` to `http/1.1` on upstream and inserts `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-SSL` headers which may trigger some middleware to close streams.

Alex Chen: On our side, confirm the endpoint allows long-lived SSE and doesn't enforce server-side idle limits. I checked the config: default idle timeout is 15m, so server isn't closing. So it's almost certainly the proxy. Action items: (a) ask Acme to raise `h2-connection-idle-timeout` to 15m or enable `raw_connect_passthrough` for that route; (b) ask them to test `curl --http1.1` as a workaround; (c) collect a full tcpdump for the period with proxy logs showing why it issued FIN (BlueGate admin logs usually show TTL/idle timeouts).

Maria Gomez: I'll pass these to the customer and request their BlueGate admin logs. They asked whether we can detect and auto-fallback to http/1.1 when we see proxy h2 translation. Is that feasible?

Samir Patel: We could add heuristics in the Private/VPC agent: if we detect repeated RST_STREAM or intermediate FINs correlated with ALPN/h2, mark the route as 'proxy-h2-problem' and route requests using HTTP/1.1 CONNECT for that customer. But that's a product change; for now doc a recommended mitigation.

connect-bot: Case #54321 created for AcmeRetail — escalation to eng-runtime flagged.

Alex Chen: For the engineering ticket, include these items: tcpdump + BlueGate admin logs + curl reproducer. Note we should not log customer tokens — ask customer to rotate keys after test. Also add a short test script to reproduce via a public proxy we control to validate mitigation.

Maria Gomez: Thanks. I'll update the case with logs and the workaround and propose a follow-up to product about automated fallback. Closing here unless eng needs more info. :thumbsup:
